quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down on a public road and you need to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are and turn on your hazard lights.
Stop where you are and hold down your horn.
Pull off the right side of the road and turn on your hazard lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the right side of the road and turn on your hazard lights.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down on a public road, pull off the right side of the road if possible. Turn on your hazard lights so other drivers can see you while you wait for help.

questions.question: What sign is this?

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. You must be ready to slow down or stop when you see a yield sign.

questions.question: How should you give the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights?

options.text: Drive to the right edge of the road as close as possible and stop.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Stop immediately, even if you are in an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right edge of the road as close as possible and stop.
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using its siren and flashing lights. Drive to the right edge of the road and stop. Avoid stopping in an intersection. You can move again after the emergency vehicle passes.

questions.question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?

options.text: When the driver you passed signals for you to return.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Before returning to your lane, make sure you have enough space from the vehicle you passed. When you can see both headlights in your rearview mirror, you have enough room to return to your lane safely.

questions.question: What should drivers check to see objects in their blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Only the left outside mirror.
Over their left or right shoulder.
Only the inside rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over their left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. Look over the appropriate shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: When turning left from a multilane one-way street to another one-way street, which lane should you start from?

options.text: Any lane, as long as it is safe.
The leftmost lane, closest to the left curb.
The center lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leftmost lane, closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, start your turn from the far left lane.

questions.question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Pull off the road.
Keep your speed and position the same.
Slow down to let the other driver safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to let the other driver safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Slow down to help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely. This helps everyone avoid dangers ahead.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the lap belt.
Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
Use only the shoulder belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap belt and shoulder belt.
questions.explanation: Always wear both the lap belt and shoulder belt. Using only one part greatly reduces your protection. Even with an automatic shoulder belt, you must also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: When can you drive off the road to pass another vehicle?

options.text: If the vehicle ahead is turning left.
If there are two or more lanes in your direction.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You may never drive off the road or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: Who must drivers turning left yield to?

options.text: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
Passing cars.
No one in particular.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming vehicles traveling straight or turning right.
questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to all vehicles coming from the opposite direction, including bicycles and motorcycles.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, what should you do?

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as possible.
Do not tailgate. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not tailgate. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep space between your vehicle and traffic barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and never tailgate.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change your speed and direction slowly and carefully.
Drive the same way you would in normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your speed and direction slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, make all speed and direction changes slowly. Never use cruise control on snow or ice. Your tires may lose grip on the road, and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: When you see a vehicle entering your interstate lane from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Speed up to pass them.
Change lanes to give them room to merge safely.
Ignore them because you have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to give them room to merge safely.
questions.explanation: Make room for vehicles entering the interstate. Change lanes when possible to let them merge smoothly and safely.

questions.question: What color are traffic control devices in construction work zones?

options.text: Red.
Orange.
Yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange.
questions.explanation: Orange signs are used in work zones. Be extra careful when you see orange signs, cones, or barriers on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road curves ahead.

questions.question: What should a driver do about right-of-way rules?

options.text: Assume all drivers automatically follow the rules.
Assume most drivers follow the rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Right-of-way rules are a guide, but do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always look at what is happening at the intersection. Yield your right-of-way if it helps prevent a crash.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get through the zone quickly.
Slow down and be ready to stop quickly.
Keep your normal speed through the entire zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop quickly.
questions.explanation: When entering a work zone, slow down and be prepared to stop. Follow posted speed limits and watch for workers and changing conditions.

questions.question: When preparing to turn left from a two-way street, you should drive:

options.text: Near the right side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street, be in the lane closest to the centerline. Turn just before your car reaches the center of the intersection. Do not cut across the corner. Turn into the first legal lane available.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Release the gas pedal a little to help them pass.
Press the brakes hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal a little to help them pass.
questions.explanation: If a driver wants to pass you, ease off the gas pedal to help them. You may need to slow down so they can safely return to your lane.

questions.question: Your chest should be ____ away from the center of the steering wheel.

options.text: 10 to 12 inches
5 inches
20 inches

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 12 inches
questions.explanation: Adjust your seat so you can see 12 to 15 feet ahead on the road. Your chest should be 10 to 12 inches from the center of the steering wheel. Your shoulders should be as high as or higher than the top of the wheel.

questions.question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding to the left, you should:

options.text: Not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left.
Turn your steering wheel to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle starts to skid on a wet or icy road, take your foot off the gas, do not brake, and turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is sliding. If you have anti-lock brakes, press the brake pedal firmly and steer straight ahead.

questions.question: When you are behind a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Be ready to use your horn.
Drive more slowly.
Allow a larger following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a larger following distance.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a three to four second distance behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts both you and the rider in danger. If the rider falls, you need extra space to avoid hitting them. The risk of falling is highest on wet or icy roads, gravel, and metal surfaces like bridges and railroad tracks.

questions.question: Check your rearview mirrors:

options.text: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
Only when you are slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.
questions.explanation: Do not stare at one spot while driving. Check your rearview mirrors often so you know where vehicles are near you.

questions.question: If dust or smoke is blowing across the road and you cannot see other vehicles clearly, you should drive slowly and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. Other drivers may also have trouble seeing you.

questions.question: As daylight fades, you should use your:

options.text: Parking lights.
Low beam headlights.
Emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your low beams when daylight starts to fade so others can see you. Use high beams only when driving alone with no other vehicles nearby.

questions.question: Why should you give extra space to children on bicycles?

options.text: They do not have the same reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and harder to see than adults.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Watch carefully for children near schools, bus stops, playgrounds, parks, and ice cream trucks. Be aware that children on bikes on the sidewalk may suddenly move into the road.

questions.question: In very foggy conditions, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off moisture and create glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work well with low beams.

questions.question: Before backing up your vehicle, you should:

options.text: Check behind the vehicle before getting in.
Depend only on your mirrors.
Accelerate quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind the vehicle before getting in.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before you get in. Children and small objects may not be visible from your driver's seat.

questions.question: Hard continuous braking on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels and makes you lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels and makes you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Pushing hard on the brakes on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and cause you to lose steering control. Drive at a safe speed for the conditions to avoid having to brake hard.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels have run off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to edge back onto the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently.
Brake hard and turn the front wheels sharply left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and brake gently.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle leaves the road, hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas, and brake gently. Once your speed slows, check traffic and find a safe place to return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel back sharply—this can cause you to lose control or move into other lanes.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks can you have before driving?

options.text: Three
Two
One

questions.correctAnswerText: One
questions.explanation: Do not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol. Even one drink will affect your driving ability.

questions.question: If a car is about to hit you from behind, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Release your seat belt.
Brace yourself.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release your seat belt.
questions.explanation: When hit from behind, your body will move backward. Brace yourself by pressing against your seat and putting your head against the head restraint. This prevents whiplash. Keep your hands on the steering wheel and be ready to brake.

questions.question: What should you do if you miss your exit on the interstate?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic and turn.
Make a U-turn to go back.
Continue driving and use the next exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make sudden turns into an exit lane. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This is a traffic law sign. It tells you that U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a collision.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn only to avoid collisions. Do not use it to make other drivers go faster or to express anger.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel drowsy while driving?

options.text: Try to stay awake.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: Stop at a rest area and take a nap, stretch, or switch drivers. Caffeine pills and energy drinks are not safe replacements for actual rest.

questions.question: When is it correct to use your horn?

options.text: When saying hello to another driver.
Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
When you are angry with another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to get another driver's attention in dangerous situations. This can help prevent a collision.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.
Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.
Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: At a flashing yellow light, slow down and look carefully before proceeding. You do not need to stop completely.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle loses traction on wet roads?

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: When your tires ride on water (hydroplaning), slow down gradually. Do not brake because it can make you slide more.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a car with airbags?

options.text: The front seat.
The back seat.
The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back seat.
questions.explanation: Airbags can injure young children. Children age 12 and under must sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.
